root_cause.text: The driver lacks a guard to prevent redundant enable/disable requests, causing unbalanced runtime PM usage count increments/decrements and improper hardware register access when the same sysfs enable value is written multiple times.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if (priv->count_is_enabled[count->id] == enable) goto exit;` to skip the runtime PM and hardware operations when the new enable value matches the cached state, directly addressing the described underflow/overflow and clock-off access issues.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function rz_mtu3_count_enable_write lacks a guard to check the current enable state before proceeding. When the same enable value is written repeatedly, it results in unbalanced pm_runtime_get_sync/pm_runtime_put calls and potential double initialization/termination. For enable=1, it unconditionally calls pm_runtime_get_sync and rz_mtu3_initialize_counter without checking if already enabled. For enable=0, it unconditionally calls rz_mtu3_terminate_counter and pm_runtime_put without verifying if already disabled. This matches the root cause of redundant enable/disable requests causing unbalanced runtime PM usage and improper hardware access.
